prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale:ground-only land/coastal/cryosphere imagery;predictable latency,documented quality,retained interfaces;all-environment least-privilege,strong-authentication,segmentation,audit. Mission Control Center(Bluebell/local-voice):routine authority,safety/commands/passes/anomalies/routing/handover;approved shift-role/time-limited elevation;declares continuity after technical-lead consultation,recording objective/duration/exit-criteria. Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral/legacy-logs):accepted-orbit authority;controlled ephemerides/predictions→Mission Control Center,Mission Planning System,Payload Processing Facility;quality→archive-operations queue before catalogue-validity changes. Network Control System(Lantern):circuits/routing/allocations/readiness/contact-record authority;status→Bluebell;accepted-ephemeris pointing;approved routing,logged changes;reject unreviewed transfer-time changes;Security Exception Ticket restricts transfer until approved containment. Ground Network Manager(Juniper/rosters):compatible maintenance,availability/staffing/assignments/site-triage;coordinates failover antenna/routing/firewall/schedule consistency. Antenna Deicing Notice:mandatory pre-acquisition tasks. Spacecraft Operations Team:contingencies/early-maneuvers/safety-triage;Bluebell concurrence before uplink;Pass Replay Packet verifies archived-downlink reconstruction. North S-Band Antenna(nominal),South S-Band Antenna(procedure-compatible alternate):commands/telemetry→Bluebell;Kiruna X-Band Antenna,Svalbard X-Band Antenna:bulk-downlink;all qualified tracking;recovery allocation follows availability/contact-priority. Command Validation Gateway(Osprey):independent syntax/timing/range/sequence/mode/baseline/provenance/configuration/window validation;screened burns;mask integrity/configuration/operator-approved security baseline. Cybersecurity Desk:exceptions,public-interface authentication/logging/abuse review,daily privileged-account review/blocks,security-anomaly coordination. Telemetry Ingest Service:state→command-checks;validated frames/contact/flow/gaps→operations/engineering/processing;immutable raw staging. Triage preserves volatile

New part:
S228: The readiness review board verifies that each open action from launch and commissioning has an owner, a due date, and an accepted residual risk statement where closure is not required before service start.
S229: Acceptance evidence is drawn from end-to-end rehearsals, procedure dry runs, interface verification records, capacity tests, security monitoring checks, and operator training completion records.
S230: The Mission Control Center demonstrates continuous console coverage for the agreed service hours and proves that shift handover logs contain the state needed by the incoming controller.
S231: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides readiness evidence showing that orbit products, maneuver screening, and conjunction coordination can be performed within the committed planning cycle.
S232: The Payload Processing Facility demonstrates that science product generation can be sustained during representative contact patterns without manual intervention beyond approved operator actions.
S233: The Network Control System records rehearsal outcomes for planned maintenance, station loss, degraded routing, and restoration of nominal connectivity after a simulated outage.
S234: The Ground Network Manager accepts the antenna readiness baseline only when the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna have current maintenance clearances.
S235: The Spacecraft Operations Team conducts at least one integrated day-in-the-life rehearsal that includes pass preparation, commanding discipline, telemetry surveillance, anomaly declaration, and recovery reporting.
S236: The Flight Dynamics Team conducts a separate rehearsal for missed tracking data and late orbit update availability to confirm that planning products remain usable under degraded conditions.
S237: The Payload Calibration Team validates that calibration operations are represented in the rehearsal schedule and that product quality decisions can be traced to approved engineering criteria.
S238: The Cybersecurity Desk participates in the final exercise by validating alert routing, privileged access review, and incident coordination with operations management.
S239: The User Services Portal uses the Product Hold List to prevent release of affected products until the applicable hold condition has been cleared.
S240: The Mission Planning System applies the delta note during schedule validation to ensure that contact and activity timing remains consistent with the latest operational constraint.
S241: The Backup Processing Cluster uses the Storage Watermark Snapshot to verify that recovery capacity is sufficient before it accepts routine standby responsibility.
S242: Osprey rejects any command request that lacks the approved authorization state, validation result, and operator acknowledgment required for routine service.
S243: Granite preserves the accepted archive baseline and confirms that retrieval tests meet the service objective before routine operations are declared stable.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
